questions.question: The maximum force a material can withstand and still return to its original shape when the force is removed is called the
questions.explanation: The elastic limit is the maximum stress a material can withstand and still return to its original shape when the force is removed. Beyond this point, permanent (plastic) deformation occurs.

questions.question: Hooke's law states that the extension of an elastic material is directly proportional to the
options: Applied force, provided the elastic limit is not exceeded
questions.explanation: Hooke's law states that the extension (e) of an elastic material is directly proportional to the applied force (F), provided the elastic limit is not exceeded: F = ke.

questions.question: Young's modulus of elasticity is defined as the ratio of
questions.explanation: Young's modulus (E) = stress / strain = (F/A) / (e/L) = FL/Ae. It is the ratio of stress to strain.

questions.question: The S.I. unit of stress is
questions.explanation: Stress = Force / Area = N/m² = N m-2 (also called pascal, Pa).

questions.question: Strain is the ratio of the extension of a wire to its
questions.explanation: Strain = extension / original length = e/L. It is a dimensionless quantity (no unit).

questions.question: A wire of original length 2m is stretched to a length of 2.01m. Calculate the strain.
A force of 100N is applied to a wire of cross-sectional area 2.0 × 10<sup>-6</sup>m<sup>2</sup>. Calculate the stress.
A wire is stretched by a force of 200N through an extension of 0.02m. Calculate the energy stored in the wire.
questions.explanation: Energy stored = ½Fe = ½ × 200 × 0.02 = 2 J.

questions.question: The energy stored in a stretched wire is given by
questions.explanation: The elastic potential energy stored in a stretched wire is given by ½Fe (half the product of force and extension).

questions.question: The stress beyond which a material breaks is called the
questions.explanation: Breaking stress is the maximum stress a material can withstand before it fractures or breaks.

questions.question: A material that can be drawn into thin wires without breaking is said to be
questions.explanation: Ductility is the ability of a material to be drawn into thin wires without breaking. Example: copper.

questions.question: A material that breaks with little or no deformation is said to be
questions.explanation: A brittle material breaks with little or no plastic deformation. Example: glass, cast iron.

questions.question: The point on a stress-strain graph beyond which the material deforms permanently is the
questions.explanation: The elastic limit is the point beyond which permanent (plastic) deformation occurs.

questions.question: A spring extends by 0.1m when a force of 50N is applied. Calculate its force constant.
questions.explanation: Force constant k = F/e = 50/0.1 = 500 N m-1.

questions.question: The S.I. unit of the force constant of a spring is
questions.explanation: From F = ke, k = F/e = N/m = N m-1.

questions.question: Surface tension is defined as the force acting
options: Parallel to the liquid surface per unit area
Perpendicular to the liquid surface per unit length
Parallel to the liquid surface per unit length
Perpendicular to the liquid surface per unit area
questions.explanation: Surface tension is the force per unit length acting parallel to the liquid surface, perpendicular to any line drawn on the surface.

questions.question: The S.I. unit of surface tension is
questions.explanation: Surface tension = Force/Length = N/m = N m-1.

questions.question: When the temperature of a liquid is increased, its surface tension
questions.explanation: When the temperature of a liquid increases, molecular kinetic energy increases, weakening intermolecular forces. Hence surface tension decreases.

questions.question: The rise of a liquid in a capillary tube is given by
questions.explanation: Capillary rise is given by h = 2T cosθ / (rρg), where T is surface tension, θ is contact angle, r is tube radius, ρ is density, and g is acceleration due to gravity.

questions.question: Water rises in a clean glass capillary tube because
options: The cohesive force between water molecules is greater than the adhesive force
The adhesive force between water and glass is greater than the cohesive force between water molecules
questions.explanation: When the adhesive force (water-glass) is greater than the cohesive force (water-water), water wets the glass and rises in the tube.

questions.question: Mercury is depressed in a glass capillary tube because
options: The cohesive force between mercury molecules is greater than the adhesive force between mercury and glass
Mercury has a high boiling point
questions.explanation: In mercury, the cohesive force (Hg-Hg) is greater than the adhesive force (Hg-glass), so mercury does not wet the glass and is depressed.

questions.question: The addition of detergent to water reduces its
questions.explanation: Detergents are surfactants that reduce the surface tension of water, allowing it to wet surfaces more effectively.

questions.question: Viscosity is defined as the internal friction which
options: Exists between a solid and a liquid
Exists between two layers of a fluid in relative motion
Occurs between a solid and a gas
questions.explanation: Viscosity is the internal friction that exists between two adjacent layers of a fluid moving relative to each other.

questions.question: The S.I. unit of viscosity is
questions.explanation: From F = ηA(dv/dx), η = F/(A·dv/dx). Unit = N/(m²·s-1) = N s m-2 (also Pa·s).

questions.question: A small ball falling through a viscous liquid attains terminal velocity when the
options: Viscous force equals the weight of the ball
Net force on the ball is zero
Acceleration of the ball is maximum
questions.explanation: At terminal velocity, the ball moves with constant velocity. This means the net force on the ball is zero (weight = upthrust + viscous force).

questions.question: Density of a substance is defined as its
questions.explanation: Density (ρ) = mass / volume = mass per unit volume.

questions.question: Relative density of a substance is the ratio of the density of the substance to the density of
questions.explanation: Relative density = density of substance / density of water. It has no unit.

questions.question: A body of mass 500g occupies a volume of 200cm<sup>3</sup>. Calculate its density.
questions.explanation: Density = mass/volume = 500/200 = 2.5 g cm-3.

questions.question: The pressure at a depth h in a liquid of density ρ is given by
questions.explanation: The pressure due to a liquid column at depth h is P = ρgh.

questions.question: Calculate the pressure at a depth of 5m in water of density 1000kgm<sup>-3</sup>. [g = 10ms<sup>-2</sup>]
Pascal's principle states that pressure applied to an enclosed fluid is transmitted
options: Only to the bottom of the container
Equally in all directions throughout the fluid
Only to the sides of the container
questions.explanation: Pascal's principle: pressure applied to an enclosed fluid is transmitted equally in all directions throughout the fluid.

questions.question: Archimedes' principle states that the upthrust on a body immersed in a fluid is equal to the
questions.explanation: Archimedes' principle: the upthrust on a body immersed in a fluid equals the weight of the fluid displaced by the body.

questions.question: A body displaces 0.5kg of water when fully immersed. Calculate the upthrust on the body. [g = 10ms<sup>-2</sup>]
questions.explanation: Upthrust = weight of water displaced = mg = 0.5 × 10 = 5.0 N.

questions.question: A solid floats in a liquid when its
options: Weight is greater than the upthrust
Weight is equal to the upthrust
Density is greater than that of the liquid
Volume is greater than that of the liquid
questions.explanation: A body floats in equilibrium when its weight equals the upthrust acting on it.

questions.question: A body weighs 60N in air and 40N when fully immersed in water. Calculate its relative density.
questions.explanation: Upthrust = 60 − 40 = 20 N. Relative density = weight in air / upthrust = 60/20 = 3.

questions.question: In a hydraulic press, a force of 20N is applied to a piston of area 0.02m<sup>2</sup>. Calculate the force on a larger piston of area 0.4m<sup>2</sup>.
questions.explanation: By Pascal's principle: F₁/A₁ = F₂/A₂ ⇒ 20/0.02 = F₂/0.4 ⇒ F₂ = (20 × 0.4)/0.02 = 400 N.

questions.question: The atmospheric pressure at sea level is approximately
questions.explanation: Standard atmospheric pressure at sea level is approximately 1.0 × 105 Pa (about 760 mmHg).

questions.question: The instrument used to measure atmospheric pressure is the
questions.explanation: A barometer is used to measure atmospheric pressure. A manometer measures pressure differences.

questions.question: The random motion of smoke particles in air is called
questions.explanation: Brownian motion is the random, zig-zag motion of small particles (like smoke) suspended in a fluid, caused by unequal bombardment of molecules.

questions.question: The spreading of the smell of a gas from one part of a room to another is due to
questions.explanation: Diffusion is the movement of particles from a region of higher concentration to a region of lower concentration due to random molecular motion.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT an assumption of the kinetic theory of matter?
options: Molecules are in constant random motion
Molecules attract one another with strong forces at all distances
Collisions between molecules are perfectly elastic
The volume of molecules is negligible compared to the volume of the container
questions.explanation: The kinetic theory assumes negligible intermolecular forces between molecules. Strong attraction at all distances is not an assumption.

questions.question: The molecules of a gas are
options: Closely packed and vibrate about fixed positions
Far apart and move randomly at high speeds
Closely packed but free to move about
questions.explanation: In a gas, molecules are far apart and move randomly at high speeds, with negligible intermolecular forces.

questions.question: In a solid, the molecules
questions.explanation: In a solid, molecules are closely packed and vibrate about fixed mean positions. They cannot move freely.

questions.question: Water has its maximum density at
questions.explanation: Water exhibits anomalous expansion. It has its maximum density at 4°C — it contracts from 0°C to 4°C and expands above 4°C.

questions.question: A crystalline solid is one in which the atoms are
options: Arranged in a regular repeating pattern
questions.explanation: In a crystalline solid, atoms are arranged in a regular, repeating pattern (lattice). Examples: diamond, sodium chloride.

questions.question: Which of the following is an amorphous solid?
questions.explanation: Glass is an amorphous solid — its atoms are not arranged in a regular lattice. Sodium chloride, diamond, and copper are crystalline.

questions.question: The temperature at which a solid changes to liquid at constant temperature is called its
questions.explanation: The melting point is the temperature at which a solid changes to a liquid at constant temperature.

questions.question: When the external pressure on a liquid is increased, its boiling point
questions.explanation: Higher external pressure requires a higher vapour pressure for boiling, so the boiling point increases with pressure.

questions.question: The average kinetic energy of the molecules of a gas is directly proportional to its
questions.explanation: Average kinetic energy of gas molecules is directly proportional to absolute temperature: KEavg = (3/2)kT.

questions.question: The movement of water molecules through a semi-permeable membrane from a region of higher concentration to a region of lower concentration is called
questions.explanation: Osmosis is the movement of water (or solvent) molecules through a semi-permeable membrane from a region of higher water concentration to a region of lower water concentration.
